releases.name: Anka Native 0.3.0
releases.body:
Anka Native 0.3.0 draws the tree canopies, plants and the arch beside Link's door that 0.2.2 left out, adds a 3D resolution setting, a faster Prepare on the phone and three new languages.
It is still slow: Kokiri Forest runs at about 14 fps on our test phone, and frames are slower than in 0.2.2 where the new content is on screen. The change for the Adreno 840 hang (#5) is untested because we have no Adreno 840.

"Tested on the phone" below means our only test phone: POCO F8 Pro (Adreno 830, 12 GB, Android 16 / HyperOS). "Tests only" means automated tests or a computer, not a phone.

### What is new

- **Mesh-drawn content is now drawn.** Kokiri Forest's tree canopies, grass, ferns, flowers and the arch beside Link's door, and the Deku Tree upper floor's floor that was invisible ([#6](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative/issues/6)). 0.2.2 skipped these draws on Turnip drivers. Your pack gets the needed shaders through an automatic update (see *After updating*). Tested on the phone with Anka Turnip: no draws skipped in Kokiri Forest and the Deku Tree's upper floor. Not tested on an Adreno 7xx, and not with Qualcomm's own driver.

releases.name: Anka Native 0.2.2
releases.body:
### Security fix

- **The launcher no longer takes control commands from other apps** ([#7](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative/issues/7)).
  - Before this release, any app on the phone could ask Anka Native's launcher to install or pick a GPU driver, add a game, start Prepare, or export or import a pack. These are commands meant for testing over adb.
  - The app now ignores them and shows a short message, unless you turn on **Settings › ADB control (debug)**. That switch is off by default and asks before it turns on. Turn it on only while you use adb.
  - Starting a game from a frontend works as before.

Everything else is as in [0.2.1](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative/releases/tag/v0.2.1). The full list of changes is in [CHANGELOG_ANKA_NATIVE.md](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative/blob/main/CHANGELOG_ANKA_NATIVE.md).

### Files

- `anka-native-0.2.2.apk`: the app (`dev.ankanative.android`), signed with the release key. Certificate SHA-256: `4d7443354f53a0aef11bc4df1a34ff3fc5bd6d748bbeb76fd78c80a6841f3bb0`. It installs over earlier versions and keeps your saves.
- `SHA256SUMS.txt`: checksum of the APK

releases.name: Anka Native 0.2.1
releases.body:
### Fixes

- **Prepare on the phone stopped at the end for Ocarina of Time** ([#3](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative/issues/3)): "76 of 42346 shaders did not build: no library written".

  The same 76 shaders don't build on a computer either, and the game runs without them. Ocarina of Time's profile was missing the list that tells the phone which shaders those are, so the phone counted them as failures. 0.2.1 adds the list.

  Checked on a computer with the phone's rule: the library is now written, byte for byte the one a computer makes.

  **If your Prepare stopped with this message:** update to 0.2.1, open the game's card and tap **Retry**. The shaders already translated are kept, so it only tries the 76 again and then writes the library.

### New

- **Prepare on a computer on Windows** too, besides Linux and the Mac. Setup: [android/README.md](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative/blob/main/android/README.md#the-environment).
- **[Discussions](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative/discussions)** are open. Tell us how it runs on your phone in the [device reports](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative/discussions/1) thread.

releases.name: Anka Native 0.2.0
releases.body:
**Prepare on the phone (experimental).** The app can now make a game's pack from your dump on the phone itself. You no longer need a computer.

### How

Copy your dump (or `.nup`) to the phone, open **Anka Native**, tap **Add game**, pick the dump and tap **Prepare**. The app does three things in the background, with a notification:

1. It rewrites the game's code.
2. It scans the game's files for shaders.
3. It translates the shaders.

When it is done, the game's card says Ready.

- **Keep the phone on a charger.** For Ocarina of Time, preparing takes about 3 hours and uses the CPU fully.
- If a step fails, the card says why. Its log is in `<title ID>-work/ondevice/logs` next to the dump. Preparing on a computer still works as before.

### What was tested

On a POCO F8 Pro with Ocarina of Time:

- **Code rewrite:** worked, about 3 minutes.
- **Shader scan:** worked, about 35 minutes for the game's 186,583 files. It found 42,346 shaders, as many as on a computer.

releases.name: Anka Native 0.1.1
releases.body:
A fix for 0.1.0: **Prepare on the phone looked done but made nothing to play.**

0.1.0 was built without the on-phone packer. Its Prepare ran a simulated engine: the progress finished, but the pack it made was an empty placeholder with no game code and no shaders, so Play could not start the game.

### What changed

- Without the on-phone packer, the app no longer offers Prepare. Home and the game's card now say to prepare the game on a computer (the README's [Install](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative#install) steps) and to pick that pack.
- A placeholder pack left by 0.1.0 is no longer shown as ready: the card says "No pack", and Play explains why.

Preparing on the phone itself is being worked on for a later release.

Everything else is as in [0.1.0](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaNative/releases/tag/v0.1.0): your own dump is needed, the driver is [Anka Turnip 1.0.0](https://github.com/EddizEge/AnkaTurnip/releases/tag/v1.0.0), and the RAM saver is recommended below 16 GB of RAM. Tested only on a POCO F8 Pro with Ocarina of Time.

releases.name: v0.5.13: NVN optimizations, FSR 1.0, controller rumble & Android 10 fix
releases.body:
## Persona 5 Royal Android Recomp v0.5.13

### Español
- **Optimizaciones universales NVN/Android y FSR 1.0 (PR #263):** Reducción de permutaciones de pipeline con EDS1-3, precompilación de shaders en segundo plano, pooling de staging/spill buffers, aislamiento en núcleos grandes y caché de vistas `HandleSlot` entre shaders.
- **Nuevas opciones en el Launcher (PR #264):** Añadidos toggles para escalado **FSR 1.0 (`NX_FSR`)** y **sombras bajas para Mali (`NX_MALI_LOW_SHADOWS`)**.
- **Vibración en mando físico y dispositivo (PR #252):** Soporte de rumble/vibración en Android.
- **Fix Android 10 (API 29) (#258):** Guard para `InsetsController` en dispositivos por debajo de Android 11 con fallback seguro a modo inmersivo clásico.
- **Diagonales en mando físico (#255) y swapchain FSR:** Zona muerta radial 2D para alcanzar el 100% en diagonales y resolución nativa de swapchain preservada cuando `NX_FSR=1`.

---

### English
- **Universal NVN/Android optimizations & single-pass FSR 1.0 (PR #263):** EDS1-3 pipeline permutation reduction, background shader prewarm, staging spill buffer pooling, big-core thread isolation, and cross-shader `HandleSlot` view caching.

releases.name: v0.5.12: Hide controls option, Play crash hotfix & GPU hang fixes
releases.body:
## Persona 5 Royal Android Recomp v0.5.12

### Español
- **Ocultar controles en pantalla:** Se añadió la opción en el Launcher (`NX_TOUCH_HIDE`) para ocultar los controles visuales. Los controles siguen 100% activos y funcionales al tocar la pantalla, ideal para quienes prefieren la pantalla limpia o juegan con memoria muscular.
- **Corrección de cierre inmediato al iniciar (Play crash):** Se protegió el acceso a JNI y verificación de permisos de almacenamiento en `android_main` para dispositivos cargando directo por NSP/FD (POCO X7 Pro, POCO F6, etc.).
- **Solución al congelamiento en "Preparing game":** Se limitaron los hilos del compilador de shaders a un máximo de 4 durante la importación, solucionando bloqueos indefinidos en procesadores MediaTek Dimensity 8350.
- **Corrección de cuelgues de GPU (GPU Hangs):** Se deshabilitaron las divisiones de renderpass a mitad de pase (`NX_CHUNK_IN_PASS=0`) por defecto en GPUs TBDR (Adreno 830 / Mali).
- **Corrección de texto en mensajes (IM / SNS Chat):** Se corrigió el renderizado del texto en las opciones de respuesta del chat del teléfono móvil (PR #251).

releases.name: Need for Speed: Underground - Android v1.0.7
releases.body:
- Lower CPU load during races. Vulkan reuses uploaded vertex data, shader parameters, and descriptor sets. Index data is written directly into the rendering buffer, eliminating an intermediate copy.
- Fewer draw calls. Objects with matching geometry and compatible rendering state can now be drawn together in the main pass and in reflections. Each object keeps its own position and rendering parameters.
- Faster P8 texture handling. Paletted textures now use NEON decoding, and a texture cache fix reduces redundant decoding of textures that haven’t changed.
- Lower runtime overhead. Xbox thread scheduling checks, graphics command processing, and frequently used port routines take less CPU time.
- Lower audio processing overhead. The low-pass filter processes both channels in parallel, and diagnostic calculations run less often.
- Improved 30/60 FPS switching. The selected mode is applied through D3D frame presentation while preserving simulation speed and game timers.

releases.name: Copperline 1.2.0
releases.body:
Copperline 1.2.0 is the second feature release of the 1.x series. It adds a video slot with an emulated NewTek Video Toaster 4000 and Video Flyer, an Amiga 2000 profile, a terminal display that also works over SSH, single-file web pages for floppy titles, high-density floppies and MP4 recording. The CPU core gains a long list of conformance fixes, and Copper, sprite, beam-counter and interrupt timing are corrected. It also includes every fix made on the 1.x branch since 1.1.0.

## Before upgrading

- **Netplay peers must all run 1.2.0.** Players and spectators need the same build.
- **Recreate RetroArch save states after updating the core.** The core's states carry a build fingerprint that includes the release version.

releases.name: Copperline 1.1.0
releases.body:
Copperline 1.1.0 is the first feature release of the 1.x series. Hard drives can now run at the speed of the period drives each Amiga shipped with. The MMU-less 68EC030, 68EC040 and 68EC060 are new CPU choices. The JIT is much faster on fast-RAM code and heavy disk I/O, and has a new "fastest" speed. A500 CIA, interrupt and bus timing are corrected against measurements of a real A500. It also includes every fix made on the 1.x branch since 1.0.1.

## Before upgrading

- **Netplay peers must all run 1.1.0.** Players and spectators need the same build.
- **Recreate RetroArch save states after updating the core.** The core's states carry a build fingerprint that includes the release version.
- **Desktop save states from 1.0.x still load.** The CIA chunks are migrated to their new layout. A resumed 1.0.x state continues under the corrected timing, so it can drift from what 1.0.x would have produced (a factory A500 state from 1.0.1 still renders byte-identical frames). States saved by 1.1.0 do not load in 1.0.x, which reports that the state comes from a newer Copperline.

releases.name: Copperline 1.0.1
releases.body:
Copperline 1.0.1 is the first maintenance release for 1.0. Most of it fixes problems reported against 1.0.0: an AGA display fetch error, a blitter race on fast CPUs, warm reboots on the A3000 and A4000, the 68060 FPU at reset, the copperhf hard-disk driver, and a window-resize hang on Windows. Menu settings are now remembered between launches, and screenshots save the picture as you see it.

## Before upgrading

- **Netplay peers must all run 1.0.1.** Players and spectators need the same build.
- **Recreate RetroArch save states after updating the core.** The core's states carry a build fingerprint that includes the release version. Desktop `.clstate` files still load: the save-state format has not changed, and a 1.0.0 state resumes byte-for-byte as it does in 1.0.0.

releases.name: Copperline 1.0.0
releases.body:
Copperline 1.0.0 is the first stable release. It follows two weeks of testing of 1.0.0-rc.1 and is the 23rd release since the source went public on 14 June.

This release adds Smart framing and native 1:1 screenshots, more control over where and how the window opens, VHD hard-disk images, a fix for AGA sprites that use scan-doubling, and a Check for updates button that only contacts GitHub when you press it.

## Copperline 1.0 at a glance

- **Machines:** A1000, A500, A500+, A600, A1200, A3000, A4000, CDTV and CD32, with OCS, ECS and AGA chipsets and 68000 to 68060 CPUs, FPUs and MMUs.
- **Accuracy:** the CPU and custom chips run on one colour-clock timeline, with the chip bus shared out cycle by cycle. Timing is checked against a real A1200, A4000 and CD32, and 45 test programs are compared pixel for pixel on every change.
- **Ready to run:** the open AROS ROM is bundled, as are ROMs for the A2091, A4091 and IDE boards, the CD32 FMV module and the HRTMon freezer. WHDLoad packages and Amiga programs boot directly.

releases.name: Copperline 1.0.0-rc.1: the first release candidate for 1.0
releases.body:
This is the first release candidate for Copperline 1.0. If testing does not turn up problems that need a second candidate, the next release will be 1.0.0.

This cycle brings three- and four-player netplay on the desktop, debugger watchpoints on device registers with a timed trace of CD32 drive commands, a refreshed AROS ROM, and a review of the whole manual against the program, which also found and fixed a few mismatches in the program itself.

Please try your usual games, demos and configurations with it. Anything that worked in 0.21.0 and does not work here is exactly what a release candidate is for: [open an issue](https://github.com/CopperlineHQ/Copperline/issues) with the configuration and the software involved.

releases.name: Eglantine Build 26/11/2026
releases.body:
Automatic daily build of `nx2-experimental` at `ed46267`.

## Changes since the previous daily build

39 commits since the 25/11 build. The big one is a rewrite of how ASTC textures are recompressed for Vulkan; the rest are game fixes, archive handling and recovery paths.

### Graphics — ASTC recompression is now a single pass ([#951](https://github.com/Eglantine-Community/Eglantine/pull/951))

Compressed textures no longer make a detour through a temporary RGBA8 image (decode → round trip through memory → encode). The BC1/BC3 blocks are written straight from the ASTC blocks the invocation touches, in one dispatch.

- **Much less memory moved** (`eb459b4118`). On Mario Kart World the old path held 236–851 MiB resident and pushed 74–657 MiB/s through it, over 33–180 transcodes a second. Now nothing but the blocks is written, so the decode image, its second dispatch, the barrier between them and the 64 MiB layer chunking are all gone.
- **Faster where it counts** (`3a1ce9cb1b`). An 8×8 footprint — the one these titles ship — used to decode each block up to four times over; it is one invocation per ASTC block now. A 1024×1024 level measures 2.1 ms instead of 5.2 ms on a GT 1030.

releases.name: v2.5.17 — Microsoft sign-in
releases.body:
## What's new

- **Microsoft sign-in no longer opens a blank white page** ([#3](https://github.com/FlameLaunchers/FlameLauncher-Android/issues/3)). Android's WebView puts `; wv` in its user agent, Microsoft reads that as an embedded browser and refuses the page — and what you get is not a message, it is an empty white screen. The marker is gone from the user agent now.

  Two more things the sign-in page needs were missing: cross-site cookies, which `login.live.com` relies on, and a `WebChromeClient`, without which the popups and dialogs the flow opens are silently dropped. The iOS build never hit any of this because WKWebView reports itself as Safari and handles those by default.
- **A sign-in page that fails to load now says why.** Main-frame errors were going nowhere, so a failure left the same white screen with nothing to report.

releases.name: v2.5.16 — Minecraft 26.4 snapshots
releases.body:
## What's new

- **Minecraft 26.4 snapshots start.** A version id like `26.4-snapshot-3` splits into `26` and `4-snapshot-3`, and reading that second part as a plain integer gave nothing — so 26.4 was treated as 26.0, missed the SDL and LWJGL 3.4.3 stack, and launched on LWJGL 3.3.6 instead. The game died immediately with `NoClassDefFoundError: org/lwjgl/sdl/SDLPlatform`; the cacio lines in the crash report were a consequence, not the cause. Version numbers are now read digit by digit, so snapshot, pre-release and rc suffixes no longer hide them, and five tests cover the shapes.
- Carries the previous fix as well: on Java 24 and newer the cacio java agent is skipped, because the `sun.misc.Unsafe` calls its `premain` depends on are refused there and a failing agent takes the VM with it.

releases.name: v2.5.15 — Minecraft 26.4 starts again
releases.body:
## What's new

- **Minecraft 26.4 (and anything else on Java 24 or newer) starts again.** The cacio setup loaded a java agent whose `premain` overwrites the AWT toolkit's static fields through `sun.misc.Unsafe` (`staticFieldBase`, `staticFieldOffset`, `putObject`). Those methods are refused from JDK 24 and gone in 26, and a failing agent takes the whole VM down with it — which surfaced as a cacio error at startup.

  The iOS build has always run the same cacio jars without that agent, on the same Java 25, using only `-Dawt.toolkit` and `-Xbootclasspath/a`. Android now does the same on Java 24+ and keeps the agent only for the older runtimes that still need it.

## Iron Lemon v0.3.0

**Lemon Online comes to Iron Lemon:** play a game's local multiplayer with your friends, wherever they are, in the same rooms as Lemon players. Plus recommended settings, Bramble support and the Lemon-Ade 0.0.9 driver. This is a preview release; Lemon stays the main app.

### Lemon Online
Lemon Online carries a game's **local wireless** play over the internet, so the game believes your friend's console is right next to yours, wherever they are. It works with any game that has a local wireless mode.

1. Open **Online** from the library, or from the in-game menu.
2. Create a room and share its code, or join one: with its code, from a friend's invite or from the public rooms.
3. Start the same game on every device and pick its **local wireless** mode (in Mario Kart 8 Deluxe: **Wireless Play**, not **Online**).

releases.body:
## Lemon-Project v1.7.0

**Lemon Online is here:** play a game's local multiplayer with your friends, wherever they are. Plus recommended settings for each game, everything Bramble needs to show your games, and the Lemon-Ade 0.0.9 driver.

### Lemon Online
On a Switch, local wireless play only reaches the consoles in the same room. Lemon Online puts every player in one **room** on the internet and passes the game's local wireless traffic through it, so the game believes the other consoles are right next to it, even if your friend is on the other side of the world. It works with any game that has a local wireless mode.

1. Open **Online** from the library, or from the in-game menu.
2. Create a room and share its code, or join one: with its code, from a friend's invite or from the public rooms.
3. Start the same game on every device and pick its **local wireless** mode (in Mario Kart 8 Deluxe: **Wireless Play**, not **Online**).

- **No account.** Each device gets a friend code. Nothing to sign up for.
- **Friends:** see who is online and what they play, invite them to your room. Accepting an invite opens the game.

- Effects drawn with geometry shaders are back on GPUs without geometry streams: their draws were skipped.

### Fixed
- Layered textures bound through the plain 1D, 2D and cube types no longer crash games (God Eater 3; Bayonetta on Mali).

releases.name: Lemon-Project v1.6.0
releases.body:
## Lemon-Project v1.6.0

A round of fixes from your logs and reports, plus three things you asked for: a Nintendo button layout for physical controllers, frontends that bring a game's update and DLC along, and the Immediate GPU fences back as an option for advanced users.

### New
- **Button layout** (Settings → Controls): **Nintendo** swaps A↔B and X↔Y of your physical controller in games, so each button presses what a Switch has in its place. For handhelds and controllers with Xbox-style labels. Menus, hotkeys and button mapping still see the buttons as labelled.
- **Immediate GPU fences**, for advanced users (Graphics → Advanced → Synchronization, also per game). Off by default. When on, the game hears that the GPU is done as soon as the work is queued, instead of waiting for it to finish. It can raise FPS in some games (Link's Awakening, issue #53) and makes others flicker (Garfield, Dragon Ball), which is why it stays off by default.
- **Games opened from a frontend** (Argosy, Beacon, ES-DE…) now load the update, DLC and custom settings that sit beside them in the same folder (issue #52).
- The **firmware 23.5 home menu** starts.

releases.name: Catherine port v0.1.6
releases.body:
## The sushi bar scene, fixed for real, and shadows for the first time (v0.1.5 was a wrong diagnosis)

v0.1.5 did not fix the *Kappa Heaven* scene of the second day. The black shots were gone, but the plates and the conveyor belt that pass right in front of the camera were missing, and a dark line floated across the picture. The explanation in the v0.1.5 notes was wrong. Please update.

What was actually wrong is a bug in how the port translates this game's shaders. Its vertex shaders come in two halves, and when the port joined them it converted depth twice. That had three effects in every version that used the original depth format (v0.1.0, v0.1.1, v0.1.3 and v0.1.4):

- The near clipping plane sat at half its distance, so geometry the console cuts away was drawn. In those sushi bar shots the camera is inside a wall, and the port drew that wall over the whole shot.
- The depth buffer was squeezed into half its range (0.5 to 1), so the depth of field compared its focus settings against wrong depths. This is where the blur problems of earlier versions came from.
- The shadow maps were stored with the same wrong depth, so no cast shadow ever showed.

v0.1.2 fixed the blurred close-ups in the *Golden Playhouse* cutscenes but broke other shots: in over-the-shoulder shots the person speaking came out blurred while the wall behind stayed sharp. This version goes back to the original depth format and fixes the close-ups properly.

Each camera in a cutscene carries its own focus settings. For cameras placed very close (close-ups, the title screen and the piano menus), those settings only line up with the picture when they are read as if the camera's near plane were 25 units, so the port now converts them for those cameras. releases.name: v0.1.2
releases.body:
## Cutscenes and the title screen are sharp (the real fix)

Close-ups in the *Golden Playhouse* cutscenes (the ones with the black bars) could still come out blurred from edge to edge, faces included, and the title screen looked out of focus. v0.1.1 blamed a short block of shader constants; that was wrong: the depth-of-field pass never reads those bytes.

The real cause is the depth format. The game never tells the graphics API which depth range it uses, and the port assumed the OpenGL-style one, which stores depth squeezed into 0.5–1. The game's depth-of-field planes come straight from each cutscene's data and are written for a plain 0–1 depth, so a face in a close-up landed *behind* the focus plane and the whole frame got the maximum blur. When the game does not choose, the port now uses 0–1 depth, so close-ups keep the face sharp and blur only the background, as intended.

- Checked on the Flip 2: the title screen (same shot before/after: background, piano and characters go from blurred to sharp), the host's introduction, the opening credits, the opening nightmare cutscene and the first puzzle stage, at 30 fps.

releases.name: BOTWRecompAndroid 0.5.3 (beta 49): profundidade de 16 bits, para os Huawei Maleoon
releases.body:
**Beta 49.** Uma opção nova para o formato da profundidade das sombras, que deve resolver as cenas escuras nos Huawei Maleoon.

> **Vindo da 0.5.2, não precisa compilar o código do jogo de novo**: é só instalar por cima. De versões anteriores, a tela inicial pede uma vez.

## Profundidade de 16 bits (#516, #240)

O jogo guarda a profundidade dos mapas de sombra em 16 bits (D16). O driver dos Huawei Maleoon recusava o D16 e fechava o jogo na abertura (#301). Por isso, desde a 0.4.0, o app usava D32 nesses aparelhos. Só que o D32 deixa cenas inteiras escuras: o céu fica certo, mas o terreno, as construções e os personagens quase pretos (#516). No POCO F7 Ultra, forçando o D32, a mesma cena ficou com metade do brilho.

- **Opção nova:** tela inicial > Compatibilidade do driver > **Profundidade de 16 bits (sombras)**: Automático, D16, D32 ou D24.
- **Automático nos Maleoon agora é D24**, e D32 só se o driver não aceitar o D24. No POCO, o D24 sai praticamente igual ao D16. Nas outras GPUs nada muda: continua D16.
- Se um formato não puder ser usado para tudo nesse driver, o app troca por outro que possa, e o log diz qual.

releases.name: BOTWRecompAndroid 0.5.2 (beta 48): mods de código
releases.body:
**Beta 48.** Mods que trazem código agora funcionam, e mais um crash com os alvos da Pedra Sheikah foi coberto.

> **Precisa compilar o código do jogo de novo, uma vez:** a tela inicial pede depois de instalar.

## Mods de código (#390)

Até aqui o app usava só a pasta `romfs` dos mods, que guarda arquivos do jogo, como textos, texturas e modelos. Agora ele também usa a pasta `exefs`, como o Eden, o Yuzu e o Ryujinx:

- **Patches IPS do código do jogo** (`exefs/<build id>.ips`, IPS ou IPS32): entram no código do jogo quando ele é compilado.
- **Módulos extras** (`exefs/subsdk1` a `subsdk9`, como os feitos com exlaunch): também são compilados e ficam logo depois do código do jogo, onde o Switch os coloca.

Funciona nos modos **Recompilado** e **Nativo**. O teste foi com a tradução árabe Arabic_Hesham, que forma as letras árabes e põe o texto da direita para a esquerda com o próprio código: a tela de título e os menus saem em árabe.

Como usar:
- Em Configurações > Mods > **Importar pasta de mod**, escolha a pasta do mod, a que tem `romfs` e/ou `exefs` dentro. A tela de Mods ainda fala só em `romfs`, mas as duas são importadas.

releases.name: BOTWRecompAndroid 0.5.1 (beta 47): crash dos alvos da Pedra Sheikah, movimento dos controles

O jogo guarda o alvo do Magnesis e da câmera da Pedra Sheikah. Às vezes, esse alvo é um ator que já tinha sumido, e o jogo lia a memória dele e fechava. No log isso aparecia como `accessing 0x...3f800570 in the game's code` em `main+120bc44`, na Mali e no Adreno.

- Agora um ator que já sumiu conta como "sem alvo", e o jogo segue. Quando isso acontece, o log diz `a stale actor in the target manager was ignored`.
- A correção é do [SavageWindRecomp](https://github.com/Revivedx/SavageWindRecomp) (MIT), o recomp de PC do BOTW, que achou o mesmo crash.
- Vale para o jogo 1.9.0 e 1.8.2. Na 1.6.0 e na 1.0.0 a função é diferente e ainda não foi coberta.

releases.name: BOTWRecompAndroid 0.5.0 (beta 46): amiibo
releases.body:
**Beta 46.** Agora dá para usar amiibo no jogo, sem figura física, e os menus ficaram mais fáceis de usar com o dedo.

## amiibo (#181)

Um leitor de amiibo virtual, com as 36 figuras que o jogo reconhece: as da série Zelda, o Lobo Link, e as de outras séries que dão itens.

- **Como usar:** escolha a runa amiibo e aponte para onde os itens vão cair. Depois toque **de novo no botão da runa** (no layout clássico, o L): o menu abre já na escolha do amiibo, em Controles. Escolha a figura e toque em **Encostar o amiibo**. O menu fecha e o jogo lê a figura.
- Com um controle, ou fora da runa: abra o menu e vá em Controles > amiibo.
- Cada figura dá seus itens uma vez por dia, como no Switch. Os dados de cada figura ficam salvos no app: o coração e o progresso do Lobo Link continuam entre as partidas.

## Menus no toque

- **As listas rolam com o dedo**, com inércia, inclusive as que abrem (como a de amiibo): antes era preciso arrastar uma barra de rolagem fina. As barras e os puxadores também ficaram maiores.

releases.name: BOTWRecompAndroid 0.4.13 (beta 45): correção para o travamento da Mali nas lutas
releases.body:
**Beta 45.** Uma correção para o travamento depois de alguns minutos de luta na Mali, e três mudanças de desempenho para a Mali.

## O travamento da Mali (#401)

Na Mali-G1 Ultra do #401, o jogo travava depois de alguns minutos de luta (com muitos efeitos), no modo Nativo e no Recompilado. Os logs mostravam uma thread do jogo presa percorrendo a lista de blocos livres do alocador de memória do jogo, que dava a volta.

- **A causa provável:** na Mali, o que um shader grava na memória do jogo é copiado de volta quando a GPU termina. Fora da "arena" de memória global, essa cópia era da faixa inteira, e desfazia o que o jogo tinha escrito ali no meio-tempo, inclusive os cabeçalhos e os links da lista de blocos livres, que ficam logo antes dos buffers. A 0.4.10 já fazia a cópia certa, mas só dentro da arena, que nunca liga nas Malis cujo driver oferece a importação de memória (como a G1 Ultra).
- **O que muda:** agora volta só o que a GPU mudou, palavra por palavra, e o que o jogo escreveu no meio-tempo fica. Quando isso acontece, o log diz `copy-back: a word the game wrote meanwhile kept`.

# PokePark 2: Wonders Beyond, PC and Android port (beta) 0.2.0

No game data is included: you need your own copy of the game (USA, S2LE01).

## Downloads

- **Windows** (10 or 11, 64-bit; Vulkan 1.3 or OpenGL 3.3): unzip and run PokePark2.exe. Keep the prompts and tools folders, SDL3.dll and vcruntime140.dll beside it. If you're updating, unzip over your old folder; your saves and settings stay.
- **Android** (11 or later, arm64, Vulkan 1.3): install PokePark2.apk over the previous version. Your saves stay.

## What's new

- **Languages.** Options > Gameplay > Language. English is built in. For Japanese, French, German, Italian or Spanish, choose it, then Language pack: it asks for your Japanese (S2LJ01) or European (S2LP01) disc image and makes a language pack from it. The game still runs from the USA disc. The port's own menus are translated too.
- **Audio options.** Options > Audio: music, sound effects and voices volumes, and the voices' language (English, Japanese, French or German), chosen apart from the text's.
- **Controls overhaul.**
  - Menus and minigames can be bound apart from the park.
  - Inverted look, stick dead zone and stick speed.

## Known issues

- The Wii Remote speaker, pointer and Nunchuk aren't supported; the game doesn't need them.

releases.name: The Sims 2 for Android 0.3.1-dev
releases.body:
The Sims 2 for Android **0.3.1-dev** improves Lua error handling, material creation, renderer diagnostics, texture conversion, and the launcher. Changes since **0.3-dev**, from signed source commit `a84f6585caca7a90afe140540714f879800c33bb`.

One APK includes **arm64-v8a** and experimental **armeabi-v7a**. The minimum requirements are now **Android 8.0 (API 26)** and **OpenGL ES 3.1**; the native Vulkan renderer accepts **Vulkan 1.0**. Game data must come from a compatible The Sims 2 Legacy Collection installation. Android 8.0–8.1 and GLES 3.1-only devices still need further device testing.

## Stability and startup

- Fixed the embedded MSVC `setjmp/longjmp` implementation used by Lua: returning to an error handler now unwinds the actual native call stack as well as restoring guest state. The bridge covers all 34 original setjmp call sites and both longjmp epilogues.
- Handle nested and repeated Lua errors, restore exception state, and remove jump contexts when their function returns, a C++ handler unwinds past them, or their thread ends. A jump to a function that has already returned is diagnosed.

releases.name: The Sims 2 for Android 0.3-dev
releases.body:
One APK now supports both **arm64-v8a** and experimental **armeabi-v7a**. The port requires Android 10 or later, OpenGL ES 3.2, and game data from a compatible The Sims 2 Legacy Collection installation. ARM32 also requires Thumb-2, NEON, and 4 KiB kernel pages. Android chooses the ABI, and the app unpacks the matching XZ-compressed engine on first use.

## Graphics and performance

- Fixed flickering and missing objects on Mali-G51 in OpenGL ES. The workaround defaults to on and can be changed in Advanced renderer settings. Fixed a related driver hang reproduced on Mali-T830.
- OpenGL ES compiles and links uncached shader programs in the background, reducing stalls when zooming out, rotating the camera, or changing floors.
- The in-game **Minimal Graphics** preset lowers 11 settings to reduce memory use. It saves the previous values, persists across restarts, and restores those values when switched off.
- **Android performance hints (ADPF) are off by default.** The launcher still lets you turn them on for the next game start.

releases.name: The Sims 2 for Android 0.2.1-dev
releases.body:
## What's new since 0.2-dev

- **Vulkan textures.** DXT1, DXT3, and DXT5 now use the correct BC formats on drivers that support them. This fixes colored noise on terrain, roads, and trees seen on Adreno 735 with both the system Vulkan driver and Turnip.
- **OpenGL ES.** Fixed dynamic buffer updates that could corrupt neighborhood chooser panels and text on Adreno 650 and 735, and the neighborhood HUD on Adreno 650.
- **Vulkan UI scaling.** The APK now includes precompiled SPIR-V variants for FSR 1 UI scaling for all 81 pixel shader entries and the built-in fixed-function pixel shader. Shaders outside the library, including shaders used by some mods, can still be compiled on the device.
- **Shader coverage.** The bundled library grew from 194 to 380 captured shaders and from 215 to 408 entries, including sampler variants. The updated capture tool checks bytecode hashes and records sampler variants. A strict diagnostic mode and a library format check help verify coverage.

## Install or update

Download the APK below or check for updates in the launcher. This build supports ARM64 devices running Android 10 or later and requires compatible The Sims 2 Legacy Collection game files.

releases.name: The Sims 2 for Android 0.2-dev
releases.body:
## What's new since 0.1.2-dev

- **Graphics.** The port's own OpenGL ES 3.2 and Vulkan 1.1 renderers handle Direct3D 9 calls. OpenGL ES is the default. Vulkan supports the system driver, bundled Turnip or PanVK on compatible devices, and imported drivers. DXVK has been removed.
- **Graphics settings.** Both renderers support render scaling, FXAA, MSAA, FSR 1 for the scene and interface, and the launcher’s ETC2 and ASTC texture cache. Existing FSR 3.1 selections switch to FSR 1.
- **PowerVR performance.** OpenGL ES buffer handling reduces severe frame-rate drops on affected PowerVR devices.
- **Lower-latency audio.** The game's EA SND mixer outputs directly to Android AAudio. DirectSound emulation has been removed.
- **Mods folder.** The launcher shows the folder for .package mods and lets you copy its path. Mods in subfolders are supported.
- **Touch input.** The on-screen keyboard opens when you tap previously blocked text fields, including pet names.
- **Loading screens.** Startup captions and town and lot loading animations follow the original game timing.

## Install or update

- **More free memory for demanding games.** The console's memory is one pool shared by the emulated console, the emulator itself and the graphics, and part of it was held without being used. releases.name: hakuX 1.3.0
releases.body:
Xbox Live through Insignia, and game fixes.

### Xbox Live
- **Insignia** — Settings → Network → Connection → Xbox Live: Insignia connects the console to Insignia, the revival of the original Xbox Live: Live games sign in, find matches and play online. If your Internet provider blocks Insignia's DNS server, point it at a computer running insigniaDNS instead
- **Xbox Live setup** — Settings → Network → Xbox Live setup walks you through it, one step at a time: the connection, the Xbox dashboard, registering the console with Insignia's Setup Assistant (downloaded for you), then making or recovering your account in the dashboard
- **Dashboard** — the library's Dashboard button (top left) starts the Xbox dashboard from the console's hard disk, where Xbox Live accounts are made and recovered. The first time, it installs the dashboard from a zip of its files (dashboard 5960) that you provide: hakuX doesn't include one
- **Title updates** — a game's Xbox Live update, once downloaded, starts with the game. Forza Motorsport's 60 and 120 fps mods cover its update too

### Games
- **Fable: The Lost Chapters** — the hero's face and arms are no longer black or noise

releases.name: hakuX 1.2.0
releases.body:
System link, stability and compatibility improvements.

### Network
- **System link over your network** — Settings → Network → System link → LAN: hakuX devices on the same Wi-Fi network find each other as Xbox consoles on a LAN do. Devices the network's broadcasts don't reach, on another subnet or a VPN such as ZeroTier or Tailscale, are added by address under Other consoles
- **XLink Kai** — system link over the Internet through an XLink Kai engine running on a computer on your network; its web page picks the game's arena
- **Console identity** — each console has its own serial number, network address and online key. A device whose hard disk was copied from another one offers to make itself a new identity, since two consoles with one identity can't see each other


### Games
- **Sega GT 2002** — the cars have their paint, reflections and sun highlights
- **Doom 3** — no longer crashes as its main menu loads
- **Fatal Frame II** — starts and reads its disc in the order it asks for
- **AirForce Delta Storm** — answers the controller and the on-screen controls (it ignored all input)
- **Silent Hill 2** — no longer crashes when it loads a room

releases.name: hakuX 1.1.0
releases.body:
GPUs beyond Adreno (experimental).

### GPUs
- **Mali, Xclipse and PowerVR (experimental)** — hakuX runs on GPUs other than Adreno: features they lack are replaced (BC and 4444 textures decoded up front, standard border colours, the push block in a buffer, D32S8 depth), and known driver bugs are worked around (`hw/xbox/hle/vk/quirks.c`). Burnout 3 and Mercenaries run cleanly on a Pixel 8 (Mali-G715)
- **Vulkan 1.1 drivers** — GPUs whose drivers stop at Vulkan 1.1 (Valhall Mali on older or vendor-capped drivers, Qualcomm's own older drivers, early Xclipse, PowerVR BXM) run through a compatibility layer (`hw/xbox/hle/vk/compat.c`)
- **Older GPUs without descriptor indexing (experimental)** — Bifrost Mali (G71, G72, G76, G52) and PowerVR Rogue: each draw binds its own textures, and depth is clamped in the shader where the GPU can't
- **Adreno** — unchanged: every replacement is off where the GPU has the feature.

### App
- **GPU driver** — a screen of its own (Settings → GPU driver): the system driver and the stored packages in one list, with their versions and authors. Packages are checked when added and can be deleted (deleting the one in use goes back to the system driver)

releases.name: hakuX 1.0.0
releases.body:
A new core replaces xemu's QEMU-based one.

### New core
- **CPU** — the Xbox's x86 code runs on a FEX JIT (FEXCore fork), and the Xbox kernel is reimplemented natively (`native/kernel`): no QEMU
- **GPU** — the NV2A push buffer is decoded into Vulkan (HLE, `hw/xbox/hle`). Custom drivers (Turnip) load through adrenotools; driver-specific workarounds are quirks (`hw/xbox/hle/vk/quirks.c`, `debug.hakux.quirks`)
- **Audio** — the MCPX APU runs on the core's own services (`native/dev/apu`), out through AAudio
- **Savestates** — per game, in slots, with the hard disk's files
- **Mods and cheats** — per game, from `mods/` (library long-press "Mods & cheats"): XBE patches and replaced disc files; 60 and 120 fps mods for 13 games (`mods/README.md`, generators in `tools/mods`)
- **Controllers** — each physical controller routed to a player with its own mapping; the on-screen controller adds to player 1

### New features
- **Updates** — hakuX looks for a newer release on GitHub when it starts and on demand (Settings → Updates); one found shows its notes and installs from there
- **Frontends** — a game launched from ES-DE or another frontend returns to it when it closes

# SeedlessDS 1.1 正式版

版本名为 `1.1`，版本号为 `153`。本次同时发布原包名替换版、共存版、对应源码及 SHA-256 校验文件。两版均关闭 Android 调试标志，正式版本号与发布文件名均不含 debug，测试控制面板关闭。

## 本次改进

- 修复后台存档提前完成时，完成状态被模拟线程覆盖，导致后续快速存档和读档一直被忽略的问题。
- 减少存读档结束后的多余槽位查询、成就附加档读取和目录扫描，成就校验改为流式 SHA-256。
- 拆分即时存档、游戏电池存档和其它文件的访问锁，避免后台慢存档连带阻塞游戏文件读取。后台存档线程降低优先级。
- 防止并发慢查询重新发布已失效的目录列表，修复日志时间格式化的并发访问。
- 在应用私有目录保留有大小上限的近期存读档记录，便于追查偶发卡顿。
- 保留 SoundTouch 原声音高加速、低延迟音频恢复修复，以及按 RP Duo 上下屏实际画面尺寸适配的柔和颗粒、柔和颗粒＋和 Nova 磷光点滤镜。

## 安装包选择

| 文件 | Android 包名 | 安装方式 |
|---|---|---|
| `seedless-ds-1.1-coexist.apk` | `com.seedlessds.app.debug` | 可直接更新本分支旧共存版，也可与官方版共存 |
| `seedless-ds-1.1-replacement.apk` | `com.seedlessds.app` | 原包名替换版 |
| `seedless-ds-fork-1.1-src.zip` | — | 两版对应的完整源码与构建配置 |
| `seedless-ds-1.1-SHA256.txt` | — | 安装包和源码校验值 |

共存版按用户选择保留历史包名中的 `.debug`，以支持覆盖更新，应用本身已关闭调试。两版均沿用本分支旧签名。

替换版与官方版签名不同。首次换用替换版，请先导出存档与配置，再卸载官方版并安装。直接覆盖官方版会因签名不匹配而失败。两个包名的数据各自独立，切换使用时需导入存档。

两版均支持 ARM64，最低 Android 5.0。证书 SHA-256 为 `99e2395bd7c458a577e6bc4f4c7237a7474cb20a178fad07313c2778a7943165`，沿用仓库随源公开测试签名。

## 验证范围

- 两种正式构建各 128 项应用测试通过，完成构建、Lint、包名和签名检查，并核对 `debuggable=false`、`testOnly=false` 及 `BuildConfig.DEBUG=false`。两版的应用资源和原生库一致。
- 原生回归覆盖 21 类存档故障、280 轮重复存读档及请求交错。

## Pacman suite (packaging revision 2)

Download **`termux-aether-suite-aarch64.pkg.tar.xz`** and its `.sha256` file. This is a real Pacman package:

```sh
sha256sum -c termux-aether-suite-aarch64.pkg.tar.xz.sha256
pacman -U ./termux-aether-suite-aarch64.pkg.tar.xz
```

It directly owns the native runtime and API commands and stages both APKs under `$PREFIX/share/termux-aether-suite`. Update Android apps using `aether-apks api`, then `aether-apks app`; Android confirms these updates. Existing app IDs, signatures and data paths are preserved. Shizuku and Arch images remain optional.

If you previously installed Aether commands manually, download `aether-install.py` and its checksum too:

```sh
sha256sum -c aether-install.py.sha256
python aether-install.py --adopt-legacy ./termux-aether-suite-aarch64.pkg.tar.xz
```

This backs up only the nine known unowned legacy commands and transfers ownership to Pacman. Unrelated files/packages are refused. No wildcard overwrite or editing of checksum-protected scripts is needed. Use `aether-update` for later protected upgrades, or install new suite packages with `pacman -U` directly.

releases.body:
# FusionHUD v1.1

Brings FusionHUD up to date with the HUD in [Bannerlator](https://github.com/The412Banner/Bannerlator) (main `b74261e6`). The HUD files are byte-identical copies of Bannerlator's, with only the license header added.

## New in the HUD
- **Pill size:** battery temperature as a `BAT °C` chip next to RAM, and a GPU name that is wider than the stats gets its own line across the top.
- **MediaTek GPUs:** GPU load and clock are read from MediaTek's GED nodes.
- **Charging state:** when Android reports no charge state, it is read from `/sys/class/power_supply` instead.
- **Config fix:** a config string with a single setting (for example just `hudSize=pill`) is no longer ignored.
- **Optional readouts your app can set** (nothing is drawn until you set them):
  - `setPresentedFps` — frames reaching the screen next to the game's own rate when something adds or drops frames after the game, e.g. `60→120` with frame generation or `60→45` when frames are lost.
  - `setDisplayServer` — `X11` or `Wayland`.
  - `setHdrState` — an HDR status line (`FusionHdr` codes).

# FusionHUD v1.0

**FusionHUD** is a lightweight, forkable in-game performance overlay for Android (Winlator / Wine / PC-emulation projects) — the MangoHud-inspired HUD extracted from [Bannerlator](https://github.com/The412Banner/Bannerlator) so any project can adopt it.

## What you get
- **The Fusion HUD** — one overlay, **5 tap-cyclable sizes** (Full / Tiles / Pill / Minimal / Mega) with toggleable per-metric chips.
- **A hardened, cross-vendor metric backend** — FPS + frametime graph, CPU (aggregate + per-core), GPU %/clock/temp, thermals, RAM/VRAM, battery (with the **mA/µA current-unit auto-detect** that fixes `0.0W` on OEMs like HONOR), and network — with graceful fallbacks across **Adreno · Mali · PowerVR · Xclipse**.
- **Diagnostics export** for triaging metric gaps on unusual devices.
- Composited ~1 Hz off the present path — designed not to cost frames.

## How to adopt it
- **Gradle (JitPack):** add JitPack and depend on `com.github.The412Banner:FusionHUD:v1.0` — or grab the **`fusionhud-release.aar`** attached below.

Pagurin catches up with nx2android's main branch of 2026-11-17. Three new settings, an audio output picker in the game's pause menu, and Android's Performance Game Mode.

## What's new

- Three settings for each game. Under Input, Menu button shows or hides the on-screen menu button (Back still opens the menu), and Controllers either gives each controller its own player or makes them all player 1. Under Performance, GPU turbo holds the GPU at its highest clock, always or only while frames run late.
- The pause menu's Game tab has an Audio output row. It sends the game's sound to the output you pick, such as the device speaker or Bluetooth headphones, until the game ends.
- Pagurin declares Android's Performance Game Mode. With Pagurin set to Performance, a game keeps its own frame rate instead of stepping down to 40 or 30.
- A game added with the import tool while Pagurin is open now shows its new settings and size right away. In 0.2.1 you had to reopen Pagurin.
- The group headings in a game's settings (Graphics, Input, Performance and so on) are in the app's accent colour, so the groups stand apart.
- The README is reorganised, with a Quick start first.

## Before you update

releases.name: Pagurin 0.2.1
releases.body:
Pagurin catches up with nx2android's main branch of 2026-11-11: games can use local play over Wi-Fi, and a controller's face buttons can follow their labels.

## What's new

- **Local play over Wi-Fi.** Pagurin now has the network permissions a port's host asks for, so a game whose profile turns on local play (`DM_LAN`, such as Animal Crossing: New Horizons) can reach other players on the same Wi-Fi.
- **Face buttons setting.** A game's Input settings have a **Face buttons** row: **Position** (the Switch's layout, the default) or **Label** (A is the button marked A, as on an Xbox-style controller). It's the same setting as the pause menu's Face buttons row.
- **The import tool cleans up `sysdata/` too.** A port made with `--firmware` carries system data, and running the tool again now removes what an older port left there.

## Before you update

- The Face buttons row only shows for a port made from nx2android's main branch on 2026-11-09 or later. An older port doesn't read the setting, so the row stays hidden.

releases.name: Pagurin 0.2.0
releases.body:
GPU drivers now work the way nx2android's main branch takes them, and a game can be removed from the library.

## What's new

- **GPU drivers for nx2android's main branch.** Each game picks one of three:
  - **The game's own driver** (the default): the one its port was made with (`porter port --vulkan-driver`), or the system's if the port has none.
  - **The system driver**, even for a port that brought its own.
  - **A driver you added from a file.** Pagurin carries libadrenotools itself, so this also works for ports made without a driver.
- **Remove a game** from its settings tab. You choose whether to keep its save; a kept save is picked up again if you add the game back.
- **The import tool cleans up.** Running it again removes files an older port of the game left behind in `host/`, `mods/`, `RomFS/` and `aoc/`.
- The game page shows its button hints in the same order on every tab. LB and RB are on the tab bar.

## Before you update

- Choosing a driver needs a port made from nx2android's main branch on 2026-11-03 or later. An older port still runs, on the system's driver. Port it again to choose a driver.

releases.name: Pagurin 0.1.0
releases.body:
The first release. Pagurin keeps your Android ports of games from other platforms in one app, such as those made with [nx2android](https://github.com/shirai91/nx2android), instead of a separate app per game.

## What's in it

- A library of your ports, with search and sorting.
- Settings for each game: docked or handheld mode, the on-screen gamepad, rumble, the frame rate counter and the engine's performance switches. A game only shows the settings its own host reads.
- One game language for every game. A game that doesn't have it runs in English.
- GPU drivers, added from a file and picked per game.
- Save export, import and delete. Import also takes another app's save folder or a zip.
- Games added from a PC with the import tool, or moved over from ports already installed as their own apps (AYN devices, or Shizuku elsewhere).

## Downloads

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `Pagurin-0.1.0.apk` | The app. Android 10 or later, arm64. |
| `pagurin-import.exe` | The import tool for Windows. On other systems, run `tools/pagurin_import.py` with Python 3.9 or later. |
